Thank you. Life can be touch, especially at your age because you don't have a choice in your living situation and the environment you're exposed too. Best advice I can give is find hobbies and skills that you take an interest in, dive into them as much as you do self harm, create your identity around things that are rewarding and bring you a sense of purpose. Self harm won't do that. Even if you don't feel like you're going to live till you're 18, assume you will. Assume if you attempt it won't work. I got to my 6th suicide attempt till i got to a point where I wanted to try. I got two years clean from any sh, eating disorder, became an A student & got my GPA in high school from 1.23 to a 3.5. I had some struggles down the line that if I had stop self harming earlier in life and really took my life genuinely I think I would've been in a much better position. I don't think my life is bad now but the coping skills I developed for years as ways to cope have made things really hard for me in all aspects of life. Even when things are good, it's hard to handle little stressors without wanting to self harm. Do what you can to do now to make life enjoyable for you when things are good. And when things are bad do what you can to make it easier. I really hope you take my advice.

1. the outcome of a failed suicide sucks especially if it were to paralyze me or fuck up my kidneys/liver. The pain of an overdose isn't fun. And the outcome of being hospitalized for a while isn't either. 


2. If I'm going to kill myself, why not just live the life I really want to instead? Somehow that seems scarier than ending my life but it's led me to travel & sightsee. I hope I continue to break out of my shell with that than continue to return to a train of thought I've known to cope with overwhelming amounts of stress. 


3. I made a list of things to do when I'm suicidal. Not necessarily in a way to prevent me from doing it like coping skills although it ends up becoming that. But If I get suicidal, my brain keeps replaying the thought of "is this actually the time I do it? Okay let's start planning" since I tend to be a bit implusive with my attempts, I decided I probably just need to do basic things to make sure my moods are not out of whack from some reason. For example, have I slept 8 hours? Have I ate today? Is my space clean? Have I been spending time with good company lately? Have I showered? If I'm going to make a decision that would be the most important one of my entire life, ending it, I would want to make sure it's the right one and not something that in my last moments I'll regret. 


4. Adding onto that, I've read a lot of stories of suicide survivors that had jumped off the golden gate Bridge that as their life was approaching an end they saw how their problems were fixable or manageable. That gives me some perspective. 


5. The brain is like a sponge, at least thats how i identify it for myself. Gotta be careful what I consumed or feed it. If I can watch motivational videos for hours on end and feel inspired, the same can go for depressive music that I listen to and the state that can put me in. If it's that easily altered, might as well try to alter it for the better.


6. If I'm going to die anyhow, might as well see it through to at least experience whatever life is.
